title: The Manifest
subtitle: Data Wrangling Assignment · group_by + summarise
story: Your wine ship arrives in Alexandria at first light, Pharos Lighthouse still burning gold above the harbor. You came in with a cargo — a hold of amphorae from the Aegean islands — and by the law of the port no ship may leave until two things are done: the cargo must be registered with the city, every amphora grouped by origin and accurately tallied; and the great Pharos light turned upon the ship to clear it for the open sea. The tide turns at dusk. Reconcile the manifest room by room, climb to the lantern, and swing the light onto your ship before the water leaves without you.

done.title: The manifest is reconciled!
done.body: Weigh every grape alike and it is Thasos, not Chios, that gives the truest wine — the correction goes down in the register and the tally is stamped true. Copy the code sealed into the manifest; it is your proof the cargo was judged fairly.

escapeDone.title: The light is yours!
escapeDone.body: The last seals fall into their piles, the three tallies match, and the door gives. You set both hands to the dial and turn the great beam down across the water until it finds your ship at her mooring — cleared. The tide has turned and she rides high on it; sails fill, and the Pharos light holds you all the way out of the harbour, the manifest true behind you.

Flat, limited palette: deep teal, night blue, and one warm amber flame. Soft film grain, painterly but clean with simple geometric shapes. Strong negative space, single centred focal subject. No people, no text, no lettering, no logos. Square composition.
worldPlatePrompt: This is a panorama. A sweeping 360-degree establishing view of Hellenistic Alexandria from its Great Harbour: the tiered Pharos lighthouse rising on its mole, pale marble colonnades and porticoed warehouses along a stone quay, moored wooden wine ships with furled sails, great stacks of sealed clay amphorae bedded in straw, striped market awnings and dyed cloth beyond, and the columned front of the Great Library on the rise above the city. Painterly, cinematic, warm and inviting; the teal-and-amber house palette — warm gold stone and lamplight against deep teal harbour water and cool shadow — in soft, even daylight (deliberately neither dawn nor sunset, so each room can set its own time of day). rooms.designNote: S1 · COMPUTE-THE-KEY (Type 1). group_by(type) |> summarise(mean(sulphates)) -> 'red' (0.661 vs white 0.489, +35.1%). VERIFIED against data/wine_cargo.csv 2026-08-07. Literally the class wrangling exercise — the easiest rung. Distractors: wrong-method values (global mean 0.557, count-instead-of-mean, grouped by vintage -> no difference) + 'white'. Puzzle object = the manifest desk. DOORS: hold is 'open' (your own ship, free to enter); the GANGPLANK to the quay is 'forward', so it gates on S1 — signing the first manifest line is what lets you go ashore. CLUE count_board teaches the n() / tally sigil. CLUE seal_1 is a PICKUP (amphora seal 1 of 9) — first seal in the first room, to teach the pickup habit.

plannedHotspots.label: The count-board
plannedHotspots.body:
Every amphora that comes off the ship is notched here, one cut for one jar. It is the plainest operation in the port and the first sigil a clerk learns: ⦀ the tally — how many are in this pile? Nothing about the wine, only the count.

The manifest itself is the ship's register of the cargo: one line per amphora, each carrying its island and its grape alongside the measurements taken at the press. More is written down than any single question needs, so the trick is choosing the right column.

Here is what str(wine_cargo) shows — the shape of the register:
tibble [4,000 × 13] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
 $ amphora_id      : chr [1:4000] "AMPH-0000" "AMPH-0001" "AMPH-0002" "AMPH-0003" ...
 $ type            : chr [1:4000] "white" "red" "red" "white" ...
 $ region          : chr [1:4000] "Kos" "Chios" "Kos" "Chios" ...
 $ varietal        : chr [1:4000] "Helvola" "Eugenia" "Eugenia" "Apian" ...
 $ vintage         : num [1:4000] -245 -246 -245 -245 ...
 $ fixed_acidity   : num [1:4000] 6.925 8.018 9.207 6.942 ...
 $ volatile_acidity: num [1:4000] 0.367 0.469 0.544 0.411 ...
 $ residual_sugar  : num [1:4000] 6.99 1.19 0.6 4.99 ...
 $ chlorides       : num [1:4000] 0.046 0.098 0.09 0.054 ...
 $ pH              : num [1:4000] 3.09 3.45 3.28 3.39 ...
 $ sulphates       : num [1:4000] 0.452 0.626 0.502 0.429 ...
 $ alcohol         : num [1:4000] 11.21 10.65 10.55 11.13 ...
 $ quality_score   : num [1:4000] 5.3 7.08 7.92 6.85 ...

question.prompt: The register's first line is the plain one. Reds and whites are taxed separately, and your ship must declare which of the two it carries is more heavily cured for the long crossing — the sulfur is what keeps a wine sound at sea. Which type, red or white wine, does your hold carry more heavily sulfured, and what is the average sulfur level of the more heavily sulfured one?

feedback.correct: Correct — noted in your field notebook: red is the more heavily sulphured cargo, averaging 0.66 against white's 0.49.
wrong: Split the cargo into its two types and take the average of the sulphates column within each — not one average across the whole hold.
Compare the two group averages themselves. Not how many amphorae are in each group, and not the gap between the two figures.
Two groups, one mean sulphates figure each. Report the larger of the two, and the type it belongs to.

plannedHotspots.label: The shipping-ledger
plannedHotspots.body:
The Library keeps what the harbour does not: a record of what each island actually ships. Read down the columns and the trouble is plain — the islands do not send the same grapes in the same proportions at all. One fills nine jars in ten with its noble varieties; another fills nine in ten with its common ones.

This matters because a grape carries its own quality with it wherever it is grown. So if you simply average an island's cargo as it stands, you are not measuring the island — you are measuring the mix it happened to pack. An island that ships mostly noble grapes will look splendid even if its ground is ordinary, and an island that ships mostly common ones will look poor even if its ground is the best in the Aegean.

To judge the ground itself you must stop letting the commoner grapes be outnumbered — give every grape an equal voice in each island's figure.

plannedHotspots.label: The great reading-desk
plannedHotspots.starterCode:
# The tally as the merchant would have it — the naive average, island by island.
wine_cargo |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(mean_quality = mean(quality_score)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_quality))

question.prompt:
The ledgers set the trouble down plainly: the islands do not ship the same grapes. Chios sends mostly its noble varieties and Thasos mostly its common ones, so a plain average flatters the famous name and tells you about the packing, not the ground.

The tally on the desk is the merchant's version, and it is the one you wrote in the market. Repair it so that every grape has an equal say in each island's figure — then say which island truly makes the better wine.

feedback.correct: Correct — noted in your field notebook: give every grape an equal say and Thasos leads at 7.43, with Chios falling to last at 6.26.
wrong: Work it in two stages. Take one average for each island-and-grape pairing first, so a common grape and a noble one each contribute a single figure.
Then release the grouping and average those per-pairing figures within each island — every grape now counts once, however many jars of it were packed.
Two summarise steps: mean quality per island-and-grape, then the mean of those per island. The leader is not the island that led in the market.

animate.motion: the fire-basket flames leaping and streaming sideways in the sea wind, sparks tearing off and whirling away into the dark

elements.label: The fire-basket

elements.desc: a bronze tally-board fixed to the wall beside the door, three worn sigils struck into it one under the next in a fixed order, each with a number cut deep beside it
elements.label: The bronze tally-board

elements.desc: a heavy bronze door barring the way onto the lamp platform, and set into its face a three-by-three grid of empty square sockets, each socket sized to take a flat clay seal
elements.label: The bronze door

elements.desc: beyond the barred door, the great fire-lamp itself in its polished bronze mirror-shell, mounted on a massive geared turning-dial with a long bronze handle at its rim
elements.label: The lamp dial

elements.desc: the whole dark harbour far below — the curve of the mole, the lamps of the city scattered beyond, and directly below on the near stone quay the moored ships along the wall, among them ONE clearly picked out: a single-masted wine ship with her square sail furled on the yard, dark hull, one lamp burning at her stern, lying dark at her mooring with the black water all around her, under the same night sky meeting the seam directly behind you
elements.label: The harbour far below

animate.motion: the scattered lamps of the moored ships and the city shivering and glinting far below, the black water breathing under them

variants.reveal: identical to the base view — same night, same viewpoint, same framing, same harbour, mole, city lamps and moored ships in exactly the same places — EXCEPT that the great lighthouse beam has swung down onto the quay and now holds steady on the ONE single-masted wine ship with her furled square sail: a hard bar of gold light lying across the black water and lighting her hull and rigging brilliantly, every other vessel left dark around her; no people, no lettering, no text

elements.desc: the head of the great spiral stair dropping away down into the dark of the tower toward the landing and the moored skiff far below, a lamp burning at the turn
elements.label: The spiral stair

sceneSpec.atmosphere: Night, lit almost entirely by the great fire — hot amber and white firelight raking the bronze and pale stone, deep blue-black sky and sea beyond, sparks on the wind, high and windswept; painterly, cinematic, triumphant, subtle film grain
sceneSpec.negatives: No people, no lettering, no captions, no text

rooms.designNote: ESCAPE · grid-select (mechanic #15), DATA-FREE — no CSV, no console. The lock hotspot (lantern_door) gets type 'grid' + endsEscape:true. VERIFIED KEY [size, shape, colour]. Cards = the 9 amphora seals collected all day (id·colour·shape·size·numeral): 1 Red/Round/Small/1, 2 Red/Round/Medium/2, 3 Red/Tall/Large/3, 4 Red/Squat/Small/4, 5 Blue/Round/Medium/5, 6 Blue/Round/Large/6, 7 Blue/Tall/Small/7, 8 Amber/Round/Large/8, 9 Amber/Tall/Medium/9. VERB SEMANTICS (each = group_by(trait) then reduce): n = COUNT of the largest pile; max = greatest pile TOTAL of numerals; min = least pile TOTAL. RESULT TABLE rows verb x cols trait: n -> colour 4, shape 5, size 3; max -> colour 18, shape 22, size 17; min -> colour 10, shape 4, size 12. THE QUEUE (on clue queue_board, in order): (1) max -> 17 = group by SIZE; (2) n -> 5 = group by SHAPE; (3) min -> 10 = group by COLOUR. grid items = the 3 queued steps (columns), buckets = the 3 traits colour/shape/size (rows), answer = {step1:size, step2:shape, step3:colour}. PAYOFF: solving opens the door and lights lamp_dial — a switch/dial the PLAYER turns to swing the beam onto their ship. ONE dial, ONE target, ONE motion — payoff, never a second puzzle. PICKUP RELIABILITY (Lucas 2026-08-07: NO auto-pickup): every seal clue body must end with an explicit 'add it to your notebook' instruction, every room is reachable in reverse via back doors, and the lock's wrong/locked feedback should state how many seals are in hand so a short player knows to go back.

plannedHotspots.label: The bronze tally-board
plannedHotspots.body:
Three marks are struck into the bronze, one under the next, each with a number cut beside it:

▲ 17
⦀ 5
▼ 10

Below them the metal is worn smooth, as though generations of hands have rested there while working something out.

plannedHotspots.label: The bronze door
plannedHotspots.lockedBody: The sockets are cold and the door will not stir. Whatever opens it, it is not force — and not yet.

feedback.correct: The seals settle into their sockets, the bolt turns over with a sound like a struck bell, and the bronze door swings back onto the lamp — the great dial standing waiting beyond it.
feedback.wrong: The sockets stay dark and the door holds.

plannedHotspots.label: The lamp dial

states.label: Swing the beam onto your ship

plannedHotspots.hint: The great lamp rides on its geared dial, the whole weight of it turning on a single bronze handle. Below, your ship lies dark at her mooring on the turning tide.
plannedHotspots.lockedBody: The lamp turns on its dial beyond the bronze door, out of reach — the door is still shut between you and it.

entry.title: The lantern
entry.text: The skiff grinds against the sea-steps and you make her fast. Above you the tower goes up and up, and the climb is long — flight after flight in the dark, with the fire roaring somewhere over your head and the whole harbour dropping away below.
